## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the operation, calibration verification, and
maintenance of the Thermo Scientific NanoDrop One micro-volume
UV-Vis spectrophotometer. The NanoDrop measures nucleic acid and
protein concentrations from samples as small as 1--2 uL and provides
absorbance ratios (A~260~/A~280~ and A~260~/A~230~) used to assess
sample purity. For the role of NanoDrop measurements within the DNA
extraction workflow, see
[SOP-L700 DNA Extraction](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd).


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of the NanoDrop One spectrophotometer in the
  EA Program laboratory, including nucleic acid quantification, protein
  quantification (A~280~ method), and custom wavelength measurements
- **Does not apply to:** Cuvette-based spectrophotometers (see
  [SOP-L201](SOP-L201-spectrophotometer-operation.qmd)), fluorometric
  quantification (see [SOP-L213](SOP-L213-qubit-fluorometer.qmd)), or
  Hach benchtop spectrophotometry (see
  [SOP-L215](SOP-L215-hach-dr3900.qmd))
- **Location:** Instrument bench, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, authorize instrument access    |
| Lab Manager       | Schedule maintenance, manage software updates |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report malfunctions        |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Optical:** The NanoDrop uses a pulsed xenon flash lamp. Do not look
  directly into the light source when the pedestal arm is open.
- **Biological:** Samples may contain hazardous biological material.
  Treat all samples as potentially infectious.
- **Chemical:** Cleaning solvents (e.g., 0.5 M HCl for decontamination)
  require appropriate handling.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Procedures

For biological spills on or near the instrument, clean and disinfect per
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd). If liquid
enters the instrument housing, disconnect power immediately and contact
the lab manager.


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                          | Location         | Notes                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------|:-------------------------------|
| NanoDrop One spectrophotometer | Instrument bench, SGM 133 | Thermo Scientific |
| Connected laptop or NanoDrop display | Instrument bench | For data export     |

### Consumables

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Lint-free wipes (Kimtech)     | For pedestal cleaning between samples     |
| Nuclease-free water           | For blanking and pedestal cleaning         |
| Elution buffer                | Must match the buffer used in extraction   |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Startup

1. Open the NanoDrop One software (or wake the integrated touchscreen)
2. Select the appropriate application (e.g., **Nucleic Acid**,
   **Protein A280**, or **UV-Vis**)
3. Clean the upper and lower pedestals with 2 uL of nuclease-free
   water; wipe with a lint-free tissue
4. Perform a blank measurement (see Section 6.2)

### 6.2 Blanking

1. Pipette 2 uL of the blank solution onto the lower pedestal. The
   blank must match the sample matrix -- use the same elution buffer or
   solvent that the samples are dissolved in.
2. Lower the sampling arm and tap **Blank**
3. Verify that the blank spectrum is flat and the baseline absorbance
   at 260 nm is near zero
4. Wipe both pedestals with a lint-free tissue

::: {.callout-tip}
Re-blank whenever you switch sample types, change buffers, or if the
instrument has been idle for more than 30 minutes.
:::

### 6.3 Measuring Samples

1. Pipette 2 uL of sample onto the lower pedestal
2. Lower the sampling arm and tap **Measure**
3. Record the following for each sample:
   - Concentration (ng/uL)
   - A~260~/A~280~ ratio
   - A~260~/A~230~ ratio
4. Wipe both pedestals with a lint-free tissue between every sample
5. Repeat for all samples

### 6.4 Interpreting Results

| Parameter       | Expected Range | Interpretation                              |
|:----------------|:---------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| A~260~/A~280~   | 1.8--2.0       | Values below 1.8 suggest protein or phenol contamination |
| A~260~/A~230~   | 2.0--2.2       | Values below 2.0 suggest humic acid, carbohydrate, salt, or guanidine contamination |

::: {.callout-note}
For environmental DNA extracts, A~260~/A~230~ ratios are frequently
below 2.0. If the NanoDrop concentration is more than twice the Qubit
reading, the UV absorbance is likely inflated by co-extracted
contaminants; use the Qubit value for planning downstream reactions.
:::

### 6.5 Data Export

1. Save the session file (.tsv or .csv) to the designated project
   folder on the connected laptop
2. Use a consistent file-naming convention:
   `YYYY-MM-DD_NanoDrop_ProjectName.tsv`
3. Record results in the lab notebook and/or project data sheet

### 6.6 Shutdown and Daily Maintenance

1. Wipe both pedestals with 2 uL of nuclease-free water, then dry
   with a lint-free tissue
2. If protein or concentrated DNA residue is visible, clean with 2 uL
   of 0.5 M HCl, wait 10 seconds, then rinse with nuclease-free water
3. Close the software and lower the sampling arm
4. Cover the instrument with the dust cover if available


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Verify instrument performance at the start of each session by
  measuring a blank; the 260 nm absorbance should read 0.00 +/- 0.02
- If the NanoDrop and Qubit concentrations disagree by more than a
  factor of two, the NanoDrop reading is likely inflated by
  contaminants; trust the Qubit value
- *TBD -- establish a schedule for periodic performance verification
  using Thermo Scientific NanoDrop verification standards*


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used lint-free wipes          | Standard trash                           |
| Pipette tips                  | Standard trash (or biohazard if samples are hazardous) |
| Residual sample on pedestal   | Wiped and cleaned as part of shutdown    |

## 10. Training Record

Before using the NanoDrop independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Observe a trained operator demonstrate blanking, measurement, and
   data export
4. Perform a practice session (blank plus at least 5 samples) under
   supervision
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
